text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ADEVARUL
- Chase Manhattan will give Romanian shipowners credits to buy new vessels.
- Farmers bought only 29 percent from the 100,000 tonnes of diesel oil planned for seasonal farm works, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Trade unions in the machine building sector demand an average monthly wage of 2.0 million lei.
- Some 25 percent of the former state farms will go into private hands by the end of the year, the paper says.
- Motorists in the Arad county protested against the new road tax.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Private farmers need funds and diesel oil to complete seasonal works on some 1.0 milion hectares, the paper says.
- Stocks at Azomures SA fertiliser maker amount to 15,000 tonnes.
- Renel RA electricity authority has to collect 2.59 trillion lei from its bad debtors, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania and Ukraine initialed a basic treaty "to clarify ties between the two states and set up premises for future cooperation", Romanian Foreign Ministry Adrian Severin said in Kiev.
- Bulgarian police discovered a bomb placed near the Sofia airport on the eve of an official visit by Romanian President Emil Constantinescu to the Bulgarian capital city last week.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- Bulgarian security services said the bomb was allegedly planted by members of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) and was allegedly aimed at Constantinescu in protest against Romanian authorities' measures to stop PKK activities in Romania.
- "Romania said good-bye" to North Bucovina and South Bessarabia, formerly occupied by the Soviet Union, the newspaper says in reference to the Romanian-Ukrainian treaty.
- Former Romanian gymnastics world champion Dan Grecu is in a critical condition due to food poisoning, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Severin denies that Romania has made a "historic sacrifice" by signing the treaty with Ukraine, the paper says.
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi starts official visit to Romania on Monday.
ADEVARUL

- Press crimes will no longer be punished with jail terms, Justice Minister Valeriu Stoica is quoted as saying. Such sentences will be replaced with community work or by banning journalists from media for "certain" periods of time, he said.
- The government decided to replace the communist-era identity papers with magnetic cards within the next five years.
- Romanian Jews are worried by current efforts to rehabilitate the right-wing extremists responsible for the death of 400,000 Jews in 1940-1944.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
